key_insight: ClinLens introduces a new benchmark for long-horizon clinical coding agents that must reason over linked longitudinal multimodal patient data, not just isolated QA or tables.
clinical_relevance: It highlights that clinically useful analyses need both executable code and correct temporal/cohort reasoning across EHR, notes, ECGs, chest X-rays, and echocardiograms.
method: 200 executable tasks across 5 linked MIMIC resources
4×5 taxonomy spanning patient-time scopes and analysis capabilities
Program-first synthesis with private reference workflows and automatic checks for artifacts, cohort/temporal semantics, and final answers
evidence_signal: On a fixed 126-task suite, the best of 24 model-scaffold setups reached 56.3% scope-macro STRICTPASS despite 100% EXECSUCCESS, while adapted biomedical systems peaked at 2.9%.
watch_item: High execution success can still mask incorrect clinical analysis, so relying on runnable outputs alone may overstate real performance.
paper_title: ClinLens: Towards Long-Horizon Coding Agents for Longitudinal Multimodal Clinical Data Science
